name: profile-settings-03
title: Verified profile settings
description: A creator-style profile page: handle, bio, social links, cover and accent colour, privacy switches, and email and phone changed in place with a 6-digit code.

useCases: Account settings for newsletters and creator apps
Profile pages with social links and handles
Apps that verify email and phone changes
SaaS settings pages with a settings sidebar

a11y.reducedMotion: Nothing slides, grows or shakes: popovers and new rows only fade, the code boxes don't shake on a wrong code, and spinners hold still; the code caret still blinks.

keyboard.action: Moves through the settings rail, the tabs, each field and button, the accent colours and the privacy switches
Opens “Edit handle”, “Change email address” or “Change phone number”, picks a colour, flips a switch, or saves a row
Moves between handle choices and through the country list
Types the 6-digit code; pasting a code or the browser's one-time-code autofill fills all six boxes
Closes an open popover, list or menu without changing anything

notes: The 6-digit code is one real input (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`) behind the boxes, so screen readers and autofill see a single field named “Verification code”.
Every field has a visible label; errors sit under their field, linked with `aria-describedby`, and say how to fix it. Saved, verified and handle-availability messages are polite live regions.
Accent colours are a radio group (each named, e.g. “Teal”, with `aria-checked`); privacy switches are labelled by what they show.
The current rail page and tab have `aria-current="page"`; read-only email and phone fields change only through their code popover.
Each row saves on its own: Save and Cancel appear only once that row changes, so nothing is saved by accident.
gaps: Flags in the country list are emoji; on systems without flag emoji they show as two-letter codes. (WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content)
The resend countdown updates once a second inside a polite live region, which some screen readers announce often. (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages)
